approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Person Notes should be handled as structured staff context on a person record; note type, visibility, sensitivity, and lifecycle matter as much as the note text itself.

notes: Read-only SQL verified Note and NoteType tables plus Auth surfaces used to manage note type, visibility, sensitivity, and lifecycle.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: When diagnosing a missing or exposed page, compare the page route, parent-page security, block security, and the specific user context instead of assuming the route alone controls access.

notes: Read-only SQL verified the connected instance has page, route, block, block type, Auth, and person-alias surfaces needed to inspect missing or exposed page behavior.
This does not prove a specific route or block is configured correctly.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Use Note Types to govern where notes appear, how they are categorized, and which staff roles can create or view sensitive notes; do not treat all person notes as one undifferentiated field.

notes: Read-only SQL verified Note and NoteType surfaces with permission-capable Auth rows, supporting note-type governance and visibility review.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Mobile check-in configuration depends on creating virtual check-in kiosk devices, assigning geofenced campus boundaries, and pointing the Mobile Check-in Launcher block at the correct devices, check-in configuration, theme, and areas.

notes: Read-only SQL verified Mobile Check-in Launcher attributes for devices, check-in configuration, theme, and configured areas, plus Device/DefinedValue support for kiosk device records.
This verifies the structural dependencies, not the correctness of any one configured launcher block.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: For communications work, email safeguards should be reviewed as a governance and deliverability topic, including sender policy, access, templates, and current Rock version behavior.

notes: Read-only SQL verified communication, recipient, template, medium/entity, and Auth/security surfaces used to review sender policy, access, templates, and deliverability governance.

notes: Read-only source inspection verified the Lava webhook handler matches active defined values by URL/method, reads Template and EnabledLavaCommands, and renders Lava without an explicit permission check in the inspected handler path.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: The Inspect Security page can show the source of a person's effective permission for a selected entity type and entity ID or GUID, including the parent from which an inherited rule originates.

notes: Read-only SQL verified Content Channel View/Item View block types, content channel/item tables, detail/page attributes, and Auth/page surfaces used for CMS visibility review.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Lava tools should return structured AgentToolResult values and use the dedicated filters for instructions, compact history content, metadata and Rock reference routes. approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Selected v19 connection requests can be reassigned, moved to another status, completed, updated by state, sent to a workflow or activity, and used to initiate SMS or email. approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Custom tools should use clear verb-and-entity names and intentionally shaped result types such as Lookup, List, Get, Summary, Insights, AvailableAttributes and AddOrUpdate. Tool names, parameters and bounded result shapes help the model choose correctly and avoid filling its context window with unnecessary data.

source_refs.title: AI Summit: The Community's First Look at Rock's AI Agents

notes: Read-only SQL verified personalization-capable Content Channel View attributes plus page/block/Auth surfaces used to test actor state, fallback content, cache/configuration, and authorization separately.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: The summit's SQL-based Lava examples were intentionally simplified teaching examples. Production tools should prefer cache objects or entity commands when appropriate, return only needed fields, enforce authorization and consider business logic and query cost before choosing SQL.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Treat every Helix endpoint as directly callable outside its front end: validate all inputs, enforce the caller's view or edit rights, avoid GET for mutations, and sanitize query and body values before SQL use.
The Mobile Check-in Launcher page should enable the virtual kiosk devices and list the check-in configuration and areas that are valid for the campuses served by that page.

notes: Read-only SQL verified the Mobile Check-in Launcher block type and attributes for devices, check-in configuration, configured areas, theme, login/phone pages, and fallback templates.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: For public-facing Obsidian blocks beginning with Rock v14, IdKey is preferred over exposing numeric entity IDs in URLs, but the server must still authorize and validate the referenced entity.

Lava Commands can bypass Rock's built-in security and business logic, so each execution surface should explicitly enable only the commands it needs; HTML blocks start with no commands enabled unless configured.
Content Channel View adds public-safe CMS guidance: verify both content-channel configuration and page/block rendering paths when auditing what content is visible.

notes: Read-only SQL verified content channel configuration tables and Content Channel View block/page rendering attributes.

notes: Read-only SQL verified the connected instance has page, block, block type, Auth, and block attribute surfaces needed to inspect Advanced HTML block risk.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Person Profile adds people/security guidance: profile work should identify the exact tab, block, action, and data surface before troubleshooting visibility or edit access.

notes: Read-only SQL verified person/profile-adjacent page/block/Auth/note/attribute surfaces needed to identify exact tabs, blocks, actions, and data surfaces.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock evaluates an item's ordered Allow and Deny permission rules from top to bottom and applies the first rule matching the current person, so a broad deny placed above a narrower allow can block the narrower role.

Rock's agent model separates agents, skills and tools, with configuration and security boundaries at each layer. Chat versus MCP and Internal versus Public are separate design choices, and only authorized tools should be exposed to the model for the current person and agent.

notes: Read-only SQL verified the connected instance has note, note type, Auth, workflow, and reporting surfaces needed to inspect note-type context and downstream consumers.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: The summit strongly warns against allowing an agent to generate and execute arbitrary SQL at runtime because that bypasses Rock security and business logic.
